title: Latency entropy benchmarking sketch
content:
Purpose:
Short sketch exploring a simple metric — 'latency entropy' — to capture unpredictability in token-level latency and how that correlates with dollars-per-query. Goal is a compact collateral piece that product/solutions can use to explain why stable tail performance matters more than mean for many interactive apps.

Background / why: (notes to self)
- Mean latency hides burstiness: two endpoints can have identical mean but very different user-perceived experience and cost when autoscaling or prewarm is considered.
- Entropy here = a lightweight proxy derived from histogram of per-token p95/p99 slices; higher entropy -> more dispersed tail -> more headroom required -> higher sustained cost.

Quick method (sketch):
1) Collect token latency samples for a workload (n ~ 100k tokens) over 24h with session boundaries.
2) Build discrete bins: [0-10ms,10-20ms,20-40ms,40-80ms,80-200ms,200ms+].
3) Compute normalized histogram, then Shannon entropy H = -sum(p_i * log2 p_i).
4) Report H, mean, p50/p95/p99 and two cost proxies: a) amortized dollars-per-token at observed throughput, b) provisioning overhead rate (extra idle capacity needed to keep p95<=target).

Example (toy numbers from local run w/ quantized-8 model):
- Samples: 125,400 tokens across 9k sessions
- mean = 42ms, p50=28ms, p95=138ms, p99=312ms
- histogram -> p = [0.35, 0.26, 0.18, 0.12, 0.06, 0.03]
- H = 2.22 bits (higher than stable baseline ~1.7)
- dollars/token (observed) = $0.000185, provisioning-overhead = +17% (est. extra slots to hit p95<=150ms)

ASCII chart — latency distribution (tokens on y axis approximated):
  300+ms | **
 200-300 | ****
  80-200 | **********
  40-80  | **************
  20-40  | *******************
  0-20   | ***************************

Interpretation notes (draft):
- Systems with H > 2.0 tend to need significantly more warm slots to maintain a given p95 than systems with H < 1.8 even when means are similar. Suggests entropy is a compact signal for 'burstiness risk'.
- Entropy correlates with p99 cost slope: small increases in H map to amplified dollar slope near tail provisioning.
- Entropy is cheaper to compute than full percentile time-series and robust to outliers if we cap top bin (200ms+).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Experiment: compare H across different quantization levels and KV cache hit-rate slices (cold vs hot). Hypothesis: low cache hit -> higher H.
- Formalize mapping from H delta -> percent provisioning overhead via simulation (slot-based model).
- Visual collateral: convert ascii histogram into small multi-line sparkline graphic for slide.
- Check sensitivity to bin edges; try adaptive binning (log-space).

- Lina: prototype a quick slide (1 page) explaining H and a 2-case demo (low H vs high H). Due: Nov 18.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally light-weight and UX-focused; aim is a one-pager plus an appendix with reproducible bench steps. Keep wording non-technical for GTM, but include a short technical appendix for Solutions/SEs.
- I'm inclined to call the collateral 'Entropy of latency' rather than 'latency entropy' if the copy team thinks that's clearer.
